column1: # Game profile of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.9.0 = v1114112). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys / ksys, NintendoWare G3d / Ui2d / Vfx / Atk, Havok), SDK 20.5.22, NVN; modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie) + sdk.

# RomFS is almost all Yaz0 (.s* extensions) and SARC (Pack/*.pack). Shaders: Shader/*.sbfsha (BNSH) and the gsys / ksys resource packs in Pack/Bootup_Graphics.pack, the terrain resource pack in TitleBG.pack, particle effects in Effect/*.sesetlist, layouts in .sblarc

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

column1: # The 3D views' base size, docked then handheld (README.md, Render scale): what DM_RENDER_SCALE scales, shown in pixels by a front end
# the virtual gamepad starts in the 3D layout (D-pad, right stick, L3 / R3): the right stick turns the camera
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the host decides each frame's step in whole vsyncs and holds the frame that long (rewriter stubs at setWaitVsyncInterval and VFR::updateInterval,
# patches.py FRAME_STEP); 30 when 60 does not hold, game time = real time. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) saves power; 0 runs the game's own
# interval controller (with the 60 fps cuts, which also serve while the game's VFR override is set)
# Tested defaults for this game (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 27.0.1, docked, 60 fps target; GitHub issues #142 / #159): present snapshots keep the GPU from idling between frames,
# which iOS's clock governor reads as headroom (30 fps without them, a steady 60 for 300 s with them and the encode thread). Render pipelines through MTL4Compiler (now the
# only path, for every game) were first tested on the iPhone on this game: the pipeline archive, the prepare step and the hybrid pipelines (5,100 prewarm lines
# prepared in 0.28 s at start instead of compiling on first use)
# Upload batch slots (nvn_mtl.m up_slots_pick; adapted from MacNativeGames 6ecb27c1 (MIT)): the game makes about 20 new textures a frame in several upload batches, and with 3 slots
# the submit thread waited about 6 ms a frame for a slot while the GPU idled (MacNativeGames, 1.9.0 on a Mac: 50.5 fps with 3, 54.5 fps with 8 and 0.0-0.2 ms of waits). Not yet run
# on NX 18 or an iPhone: DM_NVN_WAITS=1 shows the 'upload slot' waits, DM_NVN_UP_SLOTS=3 in env.txt takes it back
# One-draw passes as compute dispatches (pass_compute, on by default; nvn_mtl.m pcm_run, dmsh_pcomp.py; pass_compute.tsv seeds the pairs): about half of the game's ~145 render passes a frame
# hold one full-screen triangle (blur, luminance and mip chains, lighting quads). Mac A/B on the Great Plateau (DM_NVN_PCM=ab): 145 -> 92 passes, GPU 10.9 -> 9.8 ms a frame
# Screen shape (patches.py): DM_SCREEN_ASPECT renders a screen taller than 16:9 in its own shape, the iPhone Duo's 1.43:1 as
# 1920x1344 with a 1280x896 layout space, the HUD at the screen's edges and 16:9's sides in view (more above and below); the iOS launcher offers it
# only the merged 1.9.0 copy is extracted; the base game's own build IDs are added when needed

# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): the game uses SetHeapSize. Starts from 13 Sentinels' partition (4 GB block = 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region) until measured
# The GPU headroom controller through the live render scale (nvn_drs_gpu.h, hle_nvn.c drs_gpu_tick): while the GPU time per frame stays over 75% of the target's frame time the
# host lowers the 3D views' factor at state +0x14 one step (0.9 to 0.5 of the side; at Render scale 1.0 the stubs take the lower of it and the game's own dynamic scale), and
# takes each step back when the GPU time per frame did not fall. Off since 2026-11-23: on the iPhone 18 Pro Max (Tears of the Kingdom, c8351b8cf, about 7 min) the factor
# held 0.5-0.6 for about 5 min with the GPU time per frame unchanged (10-11 ms, as at 1.0) and no softer picture seen, so +0x14 does not reach the views' size on the
# device; Breath of the Wild's lever is unmeasured. On again once a run shows the factor cutting the GPU time
